uncited: **Inputs:** A 3D volume dataset of size $N_x \times N_y \times N_z$.
**Outputs:** An implicit kd-tree structure defined by splitting dimensions and min/max bounds, enabling ray traversal.
- **Split Dimensions:** A precomputed array `split_dim[d]` for each depth $d$ of the tree, storing the axis (0, 1, or 2) along which the split occurs.
- **Min/Max Bounds:** For each node, store the minimum and maximum scalar values of the voxels in its subtree.
Leaves store the value of a single voxel.
**Build Base KD-Tree:** Construct a kd-tree over all voxels of the entire dataset.
**Determine Splitting Axis:** For a node covering a range of voxels, identify the dimension with the largest extent (number of cells).
- For leaf nodes: Store the scalar value of the associated voxel as both min and max.
- **Degenerate Input:** If a node has only one voxel, it is a leaf.
**Time Complexity:** Construction is $O(N \log N)$ for $N$ voxels due to recursive splitting.
Traversal is $O(\sqrt{N})$ in the worst case for coherent rays, but typically much faster due to culling.
**Strengths:** Low memory footprint, fast construction, effective culling for coherent rays.
